issues.description: Inconsistent mapping between qubit indices and MPS site indices in the two GHZ simulators: the DD solution builds the GHZ circuit by applying H to qubit q_{N-1} (target=num_qubits-1) and then applying controlled-X gates with control above target (control=qubit+1, target=qubit), matching the stated ordering q_{N-1}...q_0. The tensor-network (MPS) solution instead applies H to site=0 and then applies nearest-neighbor CNOTs from site0=0 upward (site0=site, site1=site+1), without stating whether MPS site 0 corresponds to q_0 or q_{N-1}. This makes the two parts appear to use opposite ends of the chain as the 'first' qubit under the same big-endian convention, which can confuse students when comparing results or reusing reasoning across parts.
issues.suggestedFix: Explicitly define the MPS site-to-qubit mapping (e.g., “site i corresponds to qubit q_i” or “site 0 corresponds to q_{n-1}”), and then align the GHZ circuit construction accordingly across both implementations (apply H and cascade CNOTs consistently with that mapping).
